chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Cotton Club show order; pushing Benny Carter arrangements; Doc Cheatham
summary: They list the alternating Cab and Duke shows and Thomas tries to get Cab to buy Benny Carter arrangements, praising Doc Cheatham.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, it was a routine...the shows went... Cab Calloway and Bill Robinson opened the Cotton Club downtown.
Yeah, right.
Then the next show after that was Duke Ellington and Ethel Waters.
Right.
Then Cab Calloway and Bill Robinson came back again, and did the show.
Yeah. Because I think Eddie Mallory came in there, because he was going with Ethel Waters.
He was married to Ethel Waters.
Yeah. So he came in the band with her.
He might have come in... He didn't come in with us, because we didn't...
No, he didn't come in with us.
Because I recorded with her. I have some records here, "Bread and Gravy" with Eddie Mallory and Benny Carter, and a bunch of us did...Tyree Glenn...

And I had the hardest time getting Cab... I think you helped in that, too. I had the hardest time of getting him to get some arrangements from Benny Carter. Because Benny Carter arranged so... He arranged better for saxophones than anybody I knew. And I knew Benny well, you
Thomas - 132
know, and I just had to ask him, because he was such a great musician...
Well, I thought Chu did that, because Chu was always a salesman. He always told Cab...
Yeah, well, I talked to him. I made Benny Carter bring arrangements up there and just let us hear it. Then maybe Chu and you talked him into paying...
Not me. But I know Chu talked him into swapping arrangements with Chick Webb.
Yeah, right.
But Chu was always trying to get some fresh arrangements to put in the band.

Right. So I knew that Benny was a good arranger. Because he asked me to arrange a (?) for him. I was just a half-assed arranger, but I just made the arrangements the best I could. And he was crazy about Doc Cheatham. I thought Doc Cheatham was the best trumpet player he ever heard.
Which he is. He was right!
He is.
He was right!
He's my boy. I was just thinking this today, coming over here. I wrote a thing, a growling thing for Doc to do on a record. He did it so beautifully. I was crazy
Thomas - 133
about Doc.
He could do anything. To this day right now. He's one of the most fantastic trumpet players there ever was.
I caught him when he was down at The Crawdaddy. I went to hear him.
He's really, really great. It's nice to see a great veteran like that go on. A traditional cat also. Doc is older than you and I.
Well, he just needs to record, that's all.
